metadata.title: Claude, Month End Prep.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude 'learns' a skill like month-end-prep or reads it fresh every run, using the skill's own documented mechanism (folder, SKILL.md, linear steps, determinism) as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that a Skill is a file Claude reads before it acts, not a memory it draws on.
metadata.anchor_pair: B01 -> B03 (the month-end-prep folder: SKILL.md + reference, run identically in January and June)

beats.narration_text: How does Claude learn a skill like month-end-prep? It doesn't learn it — there's no training step. It reads a file, the same one, every time it runs. So what's actually written in that file?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'How does Claude learn a skill like month-end-prep?', hesitates on 'learn', corrects to 'read', lands the real question

beats.narration_text: A Skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts, and month-end-prep is a real one: a SKILL.md file holding the whole instruction set in plain language, plus a small reference folder beside it. Nothing hidden, nothing trained — the file is the entire program, and it's the same file every single time Claude opens it.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — the month-end-prep folder: SKILL.md (accented) plus a reference folder beside it

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — a folder, not a memory
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. A folder icon labelled month-end-prep opens to reveal two items: SKILL.md (accented terracotta, the instruction set) and a reference folder beside it. A caption underneath reads 'the file is the program.' THIS EXACT FOLDER RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Inside, the steps run top to bottom. Claude reads the first step, does exactly that, then moves to the next — no branching, no skipping, unless a step itself says to. Run the file in January or run it in June, and it opens to the identical steps both times.

shot.new_visual_element: Steps executing top to bottom; JAN and JUN both pointing at the same unchanged file

production_viz.label: Same steps, top to bottom, every month
production_viz.mechanic: A numbered list of steps (1, 2, 3, ...) lights up in strict order, one at a time, left to right arrows connecting each to the next — no branches drawn. Below, two calendar tags, JAN and JUN, both point an arrow at the identical step list.

beats.narration_text: That's the guarantee: the same file, run twice, produces the same checklist — reliable, repeatable, nothing improvised. But it cuts both ways. Follow a step exactly and the close goes the same way every month. Leave something the month actually needs out of the file, and Claude doesn't invent it — the skill only ever does what the file says, never what the file doesn't.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the same folder run in JAN and JUN producing identical checklists; an 'improvises' bubble struck through

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — same file, same result, no more
production_viz.mechanic: THE B01 FOLDER RETURNS, identical. Two arrows from JAN and JUN both run through it and produce two identical checklists side by side, matched line for line. A third bubble reading 'fills the gap itself' appears off to the side and is struck through terracotta — nothing added beyond the file.

beats.narration_text: A Skill is a file Claude reads before it acts, not a memory it draws on — the same steps, every run, and never more than what the file says.

props.quote: A Skill is a file Claude reads before it acts, not a memory it draws on — the same steps, every run, and never more than what the file says.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me: 'Read the month-end-prep skill. Before you do anything, walk me through each step you're about to take, and point to the line in the file it comes from.' Watch whether every step traces back to an actual line — if one doesn't, that's Claude going past what the file says. Liam, in for Bear.
